operationalisation: [flag] 'mu_bar T ~ 400 events per side' read as E[N^side_T] = 400 under the fresh-start (B = 0) convention: mu * int_0^T (1 + Psi(t)) dt = 400 (directional: excited side; common-mode: total baseline 2 mu, E[N_tot,T] = 800); the same mu results in both regimes; int(1+Psi) Richardson-extrapolated.
[flag] rho = spectral radius of the 2x2 side branching matrix; common-mode Phi = (g/2)[[1,1],[1,1]], directional Phi = diag(g, 0).

[flag] Lift (i) 'gauss': p-point generalised Gauss-Laguerre rule (alpha = b-1) for theta in y = t0 x; x_j = y_j/t0, c_j = rho(b-1)/(t0 Gamma(b)) W_j. Matches the first 2p moments of theta (short-lag behaviour). Alfonsi-Kebaier 2024 is not on disk, so the exact AK construction is UNVERIFIED.

[flag] Lift (i-b) 'gauss_composite' (added in review rev 2; operationalisation of the plan's 'Gauss-type quadrature (Alfonsi-Kebaier)', AK 2024 not on disk; Abi Jaber-El Euch 2019 / Bayer-Breneis style): composite 1-point Gauss rule for theta on I_1 = [0, xi_1), geometric interior breakpoints xi_1 < ... < xi_{p-1} = b/t0 (top factor 1, the theta-mean, fixed a priori), I_p = [xi_{p-1}, inf); weight theta(I_j), node = theta-mean of x on I_j (preserves moments 0 and 1 of theta exactly); the single scalar xi_1 minimises the L2[0,T] error (240-point log grid on [1e-3/T, upper] + bounded refinement; p = 2: xi_1 is the only breakpoint, upper 1e3/t0; p = 1 coincides with lift (i)).

[flag] Lift (i-acero, supplementary): Acero-Plank-Zhang 2026 eq. (3) with K1 = 0, beta_j = midpoints, theta(I_j) via the regularised incomplete gamma; K2 minimises the Prop. 1 bound eps_u(K2) + T^(3/2) K2 theta([0,K2])/(sqrt(3) p) by a 400-point log grid on [1e-2/T, 1e3/t0] plus bounded refinement; eps_u(K2) = ||g(t) Q(b, K2(t+t0))||_L2[0,T] (closed form of the upper-tail kernel).

[flag] Lift (ii): outer L-BFGS-B over log-rates with bounds [log(0.01/T), log(50/t0)], analytic variable-projection gradient (envelope theorem through the NNLS optimum); starts = log-spaced on [1/T, b/t0] (p = 1: geometric mean), 8 jittered copies (sd 0.5 in log-rate, seeded), the Gauss nodes, and a warm start from the previous p; polish from the best start; inner scipy.optimize.nnls on the Cholesky factor of the exact Gram matrix (jitter 1e-14 tr G); <g, e^{-xt}> by composite Gauss-Legendre (geometric mesh). Fitted for rho = 1, weights scaled by rho.

[flag] Lift (iii): rates geometric on [1/T, b/t0] (p = 1: sqrt(b/(t0 T))); exact convex QP min ||g - g^||_L2[0,T] s.t. sum c_j/x_j = rho, c >= 0 solved by enumerating supports (KKT on each support; 2^p - 1 <= 255 candidates).

[flag] p = 0: 'p0_nhpp' m^_t(u) = mu(1 + Psi(t+u)) (THE p = 0 entry; with burn-in B: mu(1 + Psi(t+u+B))); 'p0_baseline' m^ = mu (supplementary). Their 'kernel' block holds the formal metrics of g^ = 0.

[flag] Supplementary MEAN-MATCHED variant '<lift>_mean_matched' (review Q2): same lifted kernel and history, baseline mu^ with mu^ int_0^T (1 + Psi^(s + B_cal)) ds = 400 per side (B_cal = the calibration convention of the run: 0 for B = 0 and same-mu runs, B for recalibrated runs), i.e. the lifted model reproduces the expected daily count; Dm_mm = Dm + (mu^_proc - mu_proc)(1 + Psi^(u)) evaluated exactly.

[flag] Forecast-error norm ||Dm_t||_L2[0,T-t] by the trapezoid rule on the h-grid; relative error divides by ||m_t|| in the same norm, per path and t. 'Mean over (paths, t)': equal weight on the 19 decision times, averaged within each path first; SE = across-path SD of the per-path means / sqrt(paths).
[flag] Count-error proxy (review Q8): |int_0^{T-t} Dm_t(u) du| per path and t (trapezoid), absolute (per side) and relative to int_0^{T-t} m_t(u) du; mean over (paths, t).

[flag] Bias part = ||mean_paths Dm_t||; fluctuation part = sqrt(mean_paths ||Dm_t - mean Dm_t||^2); relative versions divide by ||mean_paths m_t||; 'bias_noise_floor_abs' = fluct/sqrt(paths). N3 divides the fluctuation part by sqrt(E||m_t - E m_t||^2), the truth's own fluctuation (= the fluctuation part of p0_nhpp).
[flag] N2 = mean ||Dm_p|| / mean ||Dm_{p0_nhpp}|| (ratio of means over (paths, t)); SE by the paired delta method on per-path means.

[flag] H2 screen proxy: easy cells = b in {1.4, 1.8} x rho in {0.5, 0.8}; hard cell = (1.15, 0.95); p*_screen(tau) = min p with metric <= tau, tau in {0.10, 0.05, 0.02} for every normalisation; p = 0 entry = p0_nhpp (N2 = N3 = 1 there); '>8' counted as 9; classes flat / consistent / reversed / mixed as defined in h2_direction_check.definition. Evaluated for runs B=0, B=1 and B=10, same-mu and recalibrated.

[flag] Recalibrated burn-in (review Q4, supplementary): mu_B = 400 / int_0^T (1 + Psi(s + B)) ds (expected in-day count per side 400; common-mode total 800 with baseline 2 mu_B). The pre-registered same-mu burn-in runs are kept.

[flag] Numerical floor (review Q7): per cell, mean over (paths, t) of side*||m_R(h) - m_R(h/2)||_L2[0,T-t] where m_R(h) = Richardson(h, h/2) (production) and m_R(h/2) = Richardson(h/2, h/4), on independent histories (100 paths at B = 0, 50 for recalibrated burn-in); entries with mean ||Dm|| < 10 x floor are flagged 'below_numerical_resolution'. Upper-bound indicator: the NNLS p = 8 mean ||Dm|| per cell.
[flag] Common-mode: Dm per side = Dm_tot/2 (absolute norms halved; relative norms equal to the total's).
[flag] Lift kernel tail mass beyond Delta: sum_j c_j e^{-x_j Delta}/x_j (absolute) and as a fraction of the lift's total mass; truth: rho (t0/(Delta+t0))^(b-1) and the fraction (t0/(Delta+t0))^(b-1).
[flag] sup|g - g^| on [0,T]: maximum over the quadrature nodes plus a uniform grid of step 1e-5 T.

[flag] Resolvent error ||psi^ - psi||_L2[0,T]: psi^ exact (eigen-decomposition), psi = Richardson trapezoid solution on the h-grid, taken piecewise linear; cross terms by exact product integration. Floor ~ discretisation error of psi.

[flag] Lifted forecasts m^ are evaluated EXACTLY via the exponential filters X_j (closed-form solution of the linear ODE for E[Y_j(t+u)|F_t]); the generic Volterra route (trapezoid psi^ + trapezoid convolution) is used for the truth and, for lifts, only as a cross-check (tests; route_comparison_production_h).
[flag] True forecast: Richardson extrapolation (4 m_{h/2} - m_h)/3 of the trapezoid scheme, evaluated on the h = t0/10 grid (zeta exact at grid points).

[flag] Burn-in: immigrants Poisson on [-B, T] (fresh start at -B). Pre-day events older than 0.5T enter the true forecast through a sub-grid (every 10th fine point) + cubic-spline evaluation of their smooth excitation (error < 1e-9 relative, tested); all other kernel sums are evaluated exactly at grid points.
[flag] Common-mode side labels are drawn 50/50 after the cluster simulation; they are irrelevant to the per-side forecast because Phi is symmetric and are used only for the per-side count check.

[flag] Convergence check: same histories (same seed and mu), h_eval = h/2 (Richardson from h/2, h/4) vs h; relative change of the mean ||Dm|| (absolute) for p in {1, 4, 8}, all five lifts; target 2% from the dispatch.
[flag] Exponential-kernel resolvent test: alpha = 50, beta = 100 (time scale t0, rho = 0.5); 'rel. err' = L2[0,T]-relative and sup-relative to psi(0).

[flag] Filter-route vs generic-route tests (1e-6 relative): a moderate-rate exponential sum {1, 5, 20}/T and the production NNLS p = 4 lift of the hard cell, both at production h with the production (Richardson) generic route.

[flag] Lai claim (a) evaluated literally: part 1 = rows with beta >= 1.45 in [0.4%, 3%]; part 2 = rows with 1.07 <= beta <= 1.2 in [12%, 55%]; rows with 1.2 < beta < 1.45 are not covered by the claim and listed separately.

[flag] Storage: B = 0 cells store the per-t profile at all 19 decision times (profile_all_t) plus the 3 labelled times; burn-in runs store the 3 labelled times only. Floats in screen.json are rounded to 8 significant digits.
deviations: Discretisation: the plain trapezoid scheme at h = t0/10 FAILED the dispatch's 2% convergence target (the plan's own criterion is < 10% on regret, Stop Criterion) for these entries: {"b=1.15,rho=0.95": {"nnls_L2 p=4": 0.11018524, "nnls_L2 p=8": 0.74971914}, "b=1.8,rho=0.5": {"nnls_L2 p=4": 0.15570518, "nnls_L2 p=8": 0.74986262, "mass_preserving p=4": 0.056282521, "mass_preserving p=8": 0.23643991}}; the TRUE forecast is therefore Richardson-extrapolated from (h, h/2) -- the 'refine' branch the dispatch allowed. The evaluation grid is still h = t0/10.

Lifted forecasts m^ are computed by the exact exponential-filter route (closed-form linear ODE) instead of trapezoid on the grid. Check at production h on a fixed history (route_comparison_production_h): the Richardson grid route differs from the exact route by at most 7.7e-07 (relative L2) and the plain trapezoid route by up to 2.2e-03.
Lift (iii) mass_preserving: the exact QP leaves some weights at zero, so p_effective < p in 54 of 144 cell x p entries (p = 8 -> p_effective in [4, 5]); the lift is reported at its nominal p.

limitations: Tier 0 has no control layer: ||Dm|| is a forecast error, not regret. Regret depends on how the Riccati value map weights Dm (H1's curvature kernel K), which Tier 0 does not compute; the p*_screen proxy is NOT p* of H2, and its direction depends on the normalisation and on the burn-in convention (see h2_direction_check).

In Tier 0 the two flow regimes differ only through the count scale (common-mode total baseline 2 mu): relative errors of the bias part coincide in expectation, the fluctuation part shrinks with the count.

The B = 0 convention ignores pre-day memory; with heavy tails (b = 1.15: about half the kernel mass lies beyond T) this convention is optimistic for long-memory cells; lifts fitted on [0,T] lags are wrong at lags > T, which the burn-in runs expose.

Lift (i) is a single global Gauss rule for theta (short-lag moments only; mass captured 0.13-0.32 rho at b = 1.15); lift (i-b) fixes the top breakpoint at b/t0 a priori and optimises one scalar; neither is the verified Alfonsi-Kebaier construction (source not on disk).
The Acero eq. (3) lift uses the K2 that minimises their Proposition 1 bound; for p <= 8 that bound is ~||g|| (vacuous), so the minimiser is degenerate (small K2) and the lift is supplementary only.
The NNLS L2[0,T] fit does not see kernel mass beyond T; its total mass is not controlled (subcriticality flag reported per lift).

Lift (iii) mass_preserving: the exact QP leaves weights at zero, so its effective number of factors is below the nominal p in many entries (p = 8 -> 4 nonzero factors); the lift is reported at nominal p.
The mean-matched variant fixes the expected daily count, not the conditional mean curve; it removes the gross level bias of wrong-mass lifts but not the shape error of Psi^.
Lai Table 2 time units are unstated, so the Lai tail masses beyond Delta = 1 are in Lai's (unknown) unit.
MC SEs rest on the CLT across independent paths; at rho = 0.95 counts are strongly over-dispersed.

The burn-in runs use fewer paths and independent (non-CRN) histories; differences carry both SEs. Numerical floors use 100 (B = 0) or 50 (recalibrated burn-in) paths and are not computed for the same-mu burn-in runs.
